actions.reason: I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py and costed the candidate changes by hand. None looked likely to reach the required 1% improvement, so I made no edit and ran no evaluation. Encode already peels four digits per divmod and unrolls the loop four ways. Using a divisor of 58**5 (still a single internal digit) would cut the number of divmods by 20%, but splitting each 5-digit remainder takes more small-int operations than that saves on 32- and 64-byte payloads. Dropping the separate tail loop by padding with zero groups adds a group's worth of work for the usual payload sizes. Decode already merges lanes in O(log n) big-int steps of four operations each, and every alternative form I worked through needs more operations, not fewer. On the check path, the only safe edits are inlining scrub_input and trimming call overhead, worth roughly a few hundred instructions per round trip. That is well under 1% next to the four sha256 calls and interpreter startup. I did not want to spend an evaluation on a change I expected to fail.

journal.text:
Can encode in base58/__init__.py be made at least 1% faster without changing output? I read lines 1-316 of base58/__init__.py and lines 1-92 of lineage_bench.py to decide. Devnet test agent, base58-py lineage.

I made no edits and ran no sandbox evaluations, so there are no numbers yet. I costed the candidates by hand only. Encode already peels four digits per divmod and unrolls the loop four ways. A divisor of 58**5, which still fits in a single internal digit, would cut the number of divmods by 20%. Splitting each 5-digit remainder back into characters adds its own work, though. I did not judge the net likely to clear the 1% bar, so I stopped without submitting a candidate.

My current belief is that the encode loop is close to tuned and the cheap wins are taken. That belief rests on reading, not measurement.

Next, I should try the 58**5 divisor in a sandbox and measure the remainder split directly. The part I am least sure of is whether that split costs more than the 20% divmod saving.
